Radish Tamales

Served at: La Noche de Rabanos

Serves 6Prep 30 minCook 45 min

Radish Tamales are a unique and traditional dish served during La Noche de Rábanos (Night of the Radishes), a festive event held annually on December 23rd in Oaxaca, Mexico. This celebration features radishes carved into intricate designs, and these tamales highlight the radish's crisp flavor in a savory masa dough, embodying the spirit of the festival.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups masa harina (corn flour)
  • 1 1/2 cups warm water
  • 1/2 cup vegetable oil or lard
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 2 cups fresh radishes, thinly sliced
  • 1/2 cup chopped onion
  • 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 jalapeño, seeded and finely chopped (optional)
  • Corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine masa harina, baking powder, and salt.
  2. Add vegetable oil or lard and mix well until crumbly.
  3. Gradually add warm water, kneading to form a soft, pliable dough.
  4. In a separate bowl, mix sliced radishes, chopped onion, cilantro, garlic, and jalapeño if using.
  5. Take a soaked corn husk and spread about 2 tablespoons of masa dough evenly in the center, forming a rectangle.
  6. Place 1 tablespoon of the radish mixture on top of the masa.
  7. Fold the sides of the husk over the filling, then fold the bottom up and the top down to seal the tamale.
  8. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
  9. Place tamales upright in a steamer basket and steam over boiling water for 40-45 minutes, or until the masa is firm and cooked through.
  10. Remove tamales from the steamer and let cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • Soak corn husks thoroughly to make them pliable and easier to fold.
  • For a spicier version, add more jalapeño or a pinch of chili powder to the radish filling.
  • Serve with salsa verde or a drizzle of crema for added flavor.
